summary: A 1920s-style cupola cabin, oversized, set atop a 41-ft tower moved here from Grass Mountain in 1986; staffed each summer, rented through Recreation.gov each winter.

facts.design: Cupola-style live-in cabin (14x14 ft), replica of 1920s design, atop a 40-41 ft tower

access.note: Overnight stays by reservation on Recreation.gov; winter-only, road unplowed.

visit.trail_note: Access road not maintained for winter travel; reached by ski, snowshoe or snowmobile, 2-10 miles

events.note: Tower superstructure moved here from Grass Mountain
NHLR describes the structure as 'of recent construction (1987)'; cupola cabin built atop the relocated tower
This removal is of the earlier Logger Butte cupola, 2 miles northeast, not Warner Mountain itself

evidence.supports: recent construction 1987, cupola design, only known example on a tower this tall, NHLR registered June 18 1994, elevation 5,667 ft
evidence.quote: Although of recent construction (1987), the 41' tower is historically unique in the U.S. The 14'x14' live-in cab is a replica of the cupola design of the 1920s. Most of the cupola buildings were on the ground and a few were on short crib structures. This is the only one know to have been placed on top of a 41' tower.

evidence.supports: tower moved from Grass Mountain 1986, oversized vintage replica cupola, only known example, staffed summer + winter rental, Logger Butte cupola removed 1969, location and elevation
evidence.quote: This relative newcomer to the lookout age, Warner Ridge Lookout also takes advantage of an historic design. The superstructure came from Grass Mountain in 1986, and an oversized vintage replica of a cupola cabin was built on top. This is the only known example of a cupola placed on such a high tower. The lookout is staffed during the summer, and is on the Recreation Rental program in the winter.
Originally there was a cupola atop Logger Butte 2 miles northeast which was removed in 1969.

evidence.supports: cabin size 14x14 ft on 40-ft tower with catwalk, sleeps 4
evidence.quote: The 14x14-ft. cabin sits atop a 40-foot tower and is surrounded by a catwalk. The cabin accommodates 4 people and is furnished with one double bed that comfortably sleeps two
propane stoves for heating and cooking, cookware, dishes, and a broom and dust pan. Propane is provided.
No water or electricity is provided. Guests typically melt snow for their supply of water for drinking, cooking and washing.

evidence.supports: remote access, 10-mile road not plowed, reached by ski/snowmobile/snowshoe 2-10 miles
evidence.quote: This is a very remote location; the road to the lookout is not plowed or maintained for winter travel. The lookout can only be accessed by skis, snowmobiles or snowshoes, a distance of 2-10 miles.
Reaching the cabin on the 10-mile access road is part of the snow sport fun.
Cell service may be available from the tower depending on your service provider.
Conditions on the mountain change rapidly. You need to be evaluating conditions and weather throughout your stay. Sudden storms and high winds may make skiing and driving conditions difficult.
Guests typically melt snow for their supply of water for drinking, cooking and washing.
Guests must pack out all trash and clean the cabin before departure
Warner Mountain Lookout is the winter wonderland destination for avid winter sports enthusiasts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The tower record's 'built 1969 / removed 1969' events (sourced from firelookout_com) misattribute a sentence about the earlier Logger Butte cupola, 2 miles northeast of Warner Mountain, which was removed in 1969; that sentence is not about Warner Mountain's own structure. The current Warner Mountain tower was relocated from Grass Mountain in 1986, with the cupola cabin built on it (NHLR gives 1987).

sources.title: Warner Ridge Fire Lookout Tower
sources.publisher: firelookout.com (Rex Kamstra, photos by Gary Weber and Dave Bula)

notes_for_editor: The tower record's existing events list (built 1969 / removed 1969, sourced 'firelookout_com') appears to misread the firelookout.com page: that sentence describes the Logger Butte cupola's 1969 removal, not Warner Mountain's. I've flagged this as a resolved_conflict rather than a correction since it's the events array, not a record field, that needs fixing; recommend a human replace those two events with the 1986 relocation and 1987 build instead. Minor elevation discrepancy between NHLR (5,667 ft) and firelookout.com (5,723 ft) not worth a correction. Did not find a precise end date for seasonal staffing (current vs. historical); firelookout.com's staffing claim is undated. Fact-check 2026-10-04: Recreation.gov's own listing text gives a third elevation, 5,300 ft, for what it's worth (not cited in the story, which only cites the two register-style sources for elevation).
